[PREFERENCE] User is interested in tips on how to prioritize tasks effectively.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant recommends the Eisenhower Matrix for prioritizing tasks, which involves dividing tasks into four quadrants: Urgent & Important (Do First), Important but Not Urgent (Schedule), Urgent but Not Important (Delegate), Not Urgent or Important (Eliminate).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggests identifying clear, measurable, and achievable goals to focus on essential tasks.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant advises using a task list to categorize tasks based on priority level.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant explains the ABCD method for prioritizing tasks: A (High Priority, High Consequences), B (Medium Priority, Medium Consequences), C (Low Priority, Low Consequences), D (Low Priority, No Consequences).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant emphasizes focusing on one task at a time to avoid multitasking.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant recommends time-blocking to schedule fixed, uninterrupted blocks of time for each task.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggests eliminating non-essential tasks and learning to say "no" to tasks that don't align with goals.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant mentions the Pareto Principle, stating that 80% of results often come from 20% of efforts.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant advises regularly reviewing and adjusting the task list to focus on important tasks.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant recommends using technology like Todoist, Trello, or RescueTime to help prioritize and track tasks.
